subject: Request: Temporary extended invoice terms for EduLearn pilot
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@edulearn.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.example.com>
Cc: EduLearn Finance <ap@edulearn.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: extended invoice terms for pilot

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning — the team is excited to run the fall pilot across 120 instructor accounts. One practical blocker for us: our procurement / grant cycle means we can only commit cash on a quarterly cadence. Can Redwood support a temporary Net-90 or quarterly invoicing cadence for the initial 3-month pilot?

We are proposing:
- 3-month pilot, 120 seats, billed quarterly (invoice on day 1 of quarter)
- Payment due Net-90 from invoice date (EduLearn internal AP alignment)
- EduLearn signs the MSA redlines attached and we can execute via DocuSign

If necessary we can provide a purchase order up front; this is an operations timing ask rather than a credit issue — EduLearn is a new but creditworthy customer (we can pull references). Please let me know what information you need for an exception.

Regards,
Rajiv
Director, Strategic Partnerships
EduLearn

[attachment: EduLearn_MSA_redlines.pdf]
[attachment: edulearn-payment-plan-proposal.xlsx]

Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended invoice terms for pilot

Rajiv —

Appreciate the context and the attachments. Quick notes:
- We can consider a temporary invoicing cadence change for pilots, but anything beyond Net-60 typically needs deal desk + finance signoff.
- Two practical levers that help us approve: a signed PO for the pilot amount up-front OR a short-term security hold (credit card auth or escrow) to cover first quarter in case of non-payment.

I looped in Jonas (finance) and Marissa (AE) to confirm risk and approval path. If we can get a signed PO and confirm EduLearn's AP contact, I'll escalate to the exec deal desk for a temporary Net-90 exception for Q2 pilot billing.

Next steps: can you push the PO and AP contact to me by EOD Friday? If not, we should plan for Net-60 with a one-off credit hold.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Request: extended invoice terms for pilot

Team —

Reviewed EduLearn's proposal and the redlines. Summary of finance view:
- Customer is higher ed / nonprofit-like; risk moderate but not high.
- For a short pilot (3 months) we can approve an exception to Net-60 up to Net-90 provided one of the below is in place:
  1) Signed PO that covers the first quarter OR
  2) Credit authorization/hold for the first invoice equal to one-quarter value OR
  3) A one-time prepayment covering the pilot term.

If none of those are supplied, we should approve Net-60 only. Also recommend a 6% temporary margin hold-back credit (not a discount) to be retained until pilot completion — that protects us for usage spikes without changing list price.

If Rachel can confirm the PO or AP workflow, I can sign off and we can route to exec deal desk for a one-off Net-90 approval.

Jonas
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

[internal note: ask legal to fast-track MSA redline review if PO is present]

Subject: Re: Request: extended invoice terms for pilot — exec approval granted conditionally

Rajiv / Rachel —

Good news: after review we can grant a temporary Net-90 billing cadence for the 3-month pilot under the following conditions (approved by finance + deal desk):
- EduLearn provides a signed PO that covers the first quarter invoice prior to provisioning.
- Redwood retains a 6% performance hold (credit) from the first invoice that will be released at pilot completion if obligations are met.
- EduLearn executes the attached MSA redlines via DocuSign (link below).

Once the PO and signed MSA are in place Jonas will trigger provisioning and billing will follow the quarterly invoice schedule with Net-90 payment terms for the pilot only. After the pilot we revert to standard Net-30 unless we agree otherwise in renewal.
